meta.title: Unique Pokémon
meta.description: The hub's Unique Lab: five rotating slots of 'unique' Pokémon — species in your Pokédex reborn with bonus moves, special abilities or swapped types, rolled across four rarities. A 'Unique Pokémon detected nearby' alert tells you one is in the wild, and catching one converts it (keeping its IVs and shiny) and consumes the slot. The system is the same in both versions; EX enriches it with a bigger bonus-ability pool (44 to 63 abilities) and a different set of default exotic species.

prose.heading: Pokémon no one else can get
prose.text: A unique Pokémon is a normal species from your Pokédex, reborn with extras: bonus moves drawn from a curated pool, a special ability, or even a swapped type. They are 'dynamic' — the same species can produce a different unique mon every time it is rolled — and they are tracked through five lab slots in your save. When one is out in the wild on your current route, a 'Unique Pokémon — Detected nearby!' alert pops up, and if you catch it, it joins your party as that special set with a 'Unique Pokémon' ceremony.

prose.heading: How the lab works
prose.text: The Unique Lab hub upgrade unlocks the first three of five slots; two further slot upgrades add the rest. Each slot rolls a rarity — Common, Rare, Epic or Exotic — and a species, then counts down in in-game minutes (slot one expires fastest, the fifth slowest). When the clock hits zero the slot empties and is re-rolled at the start of your next run, so the lab is always churning. Higher rarities need higher lab upgrades: without the Epic upgrade, an Epic roll downgrades to Rare, and so on.

prose.heading: Hunting a unique
prose.text: The detection alert fires on routes only: step into a route whose wild table includes one of your active unique species and a 'Unique Pokémon — Detected nearby!' alert pops up — wild dens and legendary rooms stay quiet, but a unique can still turn up there. There's a 50/50 chance the matching wild battle is actually the unique form — it fights with its bonus moves and ability, gets the slow 'important battle' intro, and keeps whatever shiny state it had. Catch it and the conversion is respectful of your luck: IVs, shiny, gender and nickname all carry over, the mon is healed to at least half health and cured of status, your Strength Charms/Curses adjust its IVs, and the slot it came from is consumed.

records.name: Unique Pokémon (system)
records.description: Five save slots (DYNAMIC_UNIQUE_MON_COUNT 5) hold 'dynamic' custom mons: species rolled from your active Pokédex, each with a rarity and a countdown. The slots are refreshed when a run begins and ends, and any species currently on your route triggers the detection alert. The system is identical in both versions; the pools of bonus abilities and default exotic species differ.
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L814 (DYNAMIC_UNIQUE_MON_COUNT 5) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1222-1330 (slot fill/refresh logic) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L4649 (refresh at run start), L4895 (refresh at run end), L3482-3484 (countdown ticks every in-game minute) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Lab slots and upgrades
records.description: The base Unique Lab hub upgrade unlocks slots 1–3; two further upgrades ('Lab Slots') unlock slot 4 and slot 5. Each active slot counts down in in-game minutes, starting faster for lower slots: slot 1 starts at 60 minutes and each higher slot starts 30 minutes later (60, 90, 120, 150, 180 for slots 1–5), so slots expire on a rolling basis and are re-rolled at the start of your next run. Expired slots are compacted so the active unique mons always sit in the first slots.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1150-1165 (slot unlock: base lab → slots 0–2, slot 3 → SLOTS0 upgrade, slot 4 → SLOTS1 upgrade), L1301 (countdown 60 + 30 × slot), L1265-1283 (invalid slots compacted and re-rolled) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Rarity roll
records.description: Each slot roll is Random() % 7: one in seven is Exotic, two in seven Epic, two in seven Rare and two in seven Common. The result is then downgraded through any rarities your lab upgrades don't yet support (Exotic→Epic without the Exotic upgrade, Epic→Rare, Rare→Common), so a brand-new lab only ever rolls Commons until it is upgraded.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1107-1148 (RandomRarity: 1/7 Exotic, 2/7 Epic, 2/7 Rare, 2/7 Common, then downgrade chain by lab rarity upgrades) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Common
records.description: The everyday rarity: two bonus moves drawn from the curated pool. With the Unique Typings lab upgrade, a Common roll can instead be a type-swapped mon (a single random type, no bonus moves).
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1008-1012 (Common: move1+move2, original format), L1032-1034 (Common: type only, mon-type format) (identical @origin/expansion); include/rogue_gifts.h @vanilla L5-11 (rarity comments) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Rare
records.description: One bonus move plus a special ability from the curated pool. With the Unique Typings lab upgrade, a Rare roll can instead be a type-swapped mon with two bonus moves.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1014-1017 (Rare: move1 + ability, original format), L1036-1039 (Rare: type + 2 moves, mon-type format) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Epic
records.description: Three bonus moves plus a special ability — the strongest 'rolled' rarity. With the Unique Typings lab upgrade, an Epic roll can instead be a type-swapped mon with two bonus moves and a special ability.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1019-1024 (Epic: move1+move2+move3 + ability, original format), L1041-1045 (Epic: type + 2 moves + ability, mon-type format) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Exotic
records.description: The jackpot roll (1 in 7): instead of a random bonus set, the slot holds a bespoke 'Exotic' mon from the static custom pool — the special mons tied to quests and default spawns. An Exotic slot picks an unused unlocked Exotic mon, and if every one is already in play it falls back to an Epic roll. Requires the Exotic lab upgrade or it downgrades.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1107-1129 (1/7 Exotic), L1303-1314 (Exotic slot: unused unlocked exotic mon, Epic fallback), L1138-1139 (Exotic requires the Exotic lab upgrade) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1181-1220 (SelectUnusedUnlockedExoticMon: default-spawn custom mons + unlocked quest mons) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Bonus move pool
records.description: Bonus moves are drawn from a curated in-game list (the sDynamicCustomMonMoves table), excluding anything the species already learns by level-up or from tutors — so a unique mon's bonus set is always genuinely new to it. The available pool grows in EX, which adds newer-generation moves to the table.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L983-995 (query: include curated move pool, exclude the species' level-up and tutor moves) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla (sDynamicCustomMonMoves table, extended in EX) / @origin/expansion (larger table)

records.name: Special ability pool
records.description: A unique mon's special ability is drawn from a curated pool of strong abilities. This is one of the version differences in the feature: Vanilla's pool is a modest 44-ability Gen 1–3 list (Drizzle, Static, Water Absorb, Battle Armor and their peers), while EX's pool grows to 63 abilities, adding the Surge abilities, Multiscale, Protean, Magic Bounce, Regenerator and friends.

differences.vanilla: Small Gen 1–3 ability pool of 44 entries (Drizzle, Speed Boost, Battle Armor, Limber, Sand Veil, Static, Volt Absorb, Water Absorb, and similar).
differences.ex: Large Gen 1–9 pool of 63 abilities including Electric/Psychic/Misty/Grassy Surge, Prankster, Multiscale, Protean, Magic Bounce, Regenerator, Mold Breaker and more.

records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L118-161 (Vanilla pool: 44 Gen 1–3 abilities in the #else branch) / @origin/expansion L54-116 (expanded 63-ability Gen 1–9 pool behind #ifdef ROGUE_EXPANSION)

records.name: Unique Typings (lab upgrade)
records.description: A lab upgrade that changes the format of rolled unique mons: instead of bonus moves and abilities, a mon can get a swapped type — its primary type is replaced with a random one that fits its typing rules. Available from Common (type only) up to Epic (type + two moves + ability). Without the upgrade, all rolls use the standard bonus-move format.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L975-981 (mon-type format locked behind HUB_UPGRADE_LAB_UNIQUE_TYPINGS), L1028-1046 (per-rarity mon-type payloads) (identical @origin/expansion); data/hub.json (the lab upgrade's cost and requirements are documented on the Hub page)

records.name: 'Unique Pokémon — Detected nearby!'
records.description: When you enter a route, the game checks the route's wild encounter table against your active unique slots, and any match fires the 'Unique Pokémon — Detected nearby!' alert so you know a catchable unique is in the area. The check is route-only — wild dens and legendary rooms are never checked, though a unique can still appear there. Shiny and unique wilds also get the slow 'important battle' intro when you engage them.
records.source: src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L5843-5883 (route room-entry case: wild encounter table vs active unique slots, popup pushed on match — the den and legendary room cases have no such check) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_popup.c @vanilla L298-299 (alert text), L1793-1801 (popup push) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L543-547 (shiny/unique wilds are 'important battles') (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: The 50% unique wild
records.description: Not every matching wild is the unique one: when a wild mon's species matches an active unique slot, there's a 50% chance the battle uses the custom set (bonus moves/ability/type) — otherwise it fights as a normal wild. The conversion happens in place and deliberately preserves the mon's shiny state.
records.source: src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L8470-8505 (TryApplyCustomMon: only in Route/Wild Den/Legendary rooms, 1-in-2 chance, shiny preserved, wildBattleCustomMonId set) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Catching a unique
records.description: When you catch the unique form, the mon is converted to its custom set while keeping its IVs, shiny, gender and nickname. It's then healed to at least half of its max HP, cured of any status, and its IVs are adjusted by your net Strength Charms/Curses. The lab slot that produced it is consumed — that unique is now yours, not a rolling slot.
records.source: src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L1229-1280 (Rogue_ModifyCaughtMon: convert, remove the dynamic mon, heal to 1/2, cure status, IV charm/curse) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: The static custom pool
records.description: Behind the dynamic rolls sits a static pool of 37 bespoke custom mons: Kurt (a shiny Stantler), Pikin (a special Mareep), Wahey's Electrode and Wobbuffet, and a long list of 'Exotic' mons (Farfetch'd, Castform, Pikachu, Lugia and more) used as Exotic-slot fills and quest rewards. Several entries are version-gated at build time, so the default-spawn exotic species differ: Vanilla uses Chimecho, Aron, Misdreavus, Hoothoot, Azurill and Ekans, while EX uses Tympole, Burmy, Carbink, Wattrel, Shinx, Venipede and Trapinch.

differences.vanilla: Default-spawn exotic species are the Gen 1–3 set (Chimecho, Aron, Misdreavus, Hoothoot, Azurill, Ekans) and Pikin carries a Gen 3 move set.
differences.ex: Default-spawn exotic species are the newer set (Tympole, Burmy, Carbink, Wattrel, Shinx, Venipede, Trapinch), Pikin carries an EX move set with Fluffy/Teravolt, and Pikin can Mega Evolve (the Mega form is excluded from custom-mon lookups because it has its own ability).

records.source: src/data/rogue/custom_mons.json @vanilla (37 static custom mons, '#if' build-time version gates) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_gifts.c @origin/expansion L577-581 (EX-only PIKIN_MEGA exception in the custom-mon lookup — the file's only divergence, absent from @vanilla)
